name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
full_name: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (with Revised Points of Focus, 2022)
notice: Trust services criteria numbers and point of focus names are used for identification only. Criteria text is copyrighted by the AICPA; descriptions and guidance are written by HCG.

sources.title: 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised Points of Focus, 2022), TSP section 100
Trust services criteria list derived from HCG's copy (criterion IDs, groups, point of focus names and scope)
HCG plain-language descriptions and assessment guidance

scoring.summary: Share of in-scope criteria met. SOC 2 has no official score; an auditor's opinion depends on whether controls meet every in-scope criterion.

rules.summary: The common criteria (CC1 to CC9) always apply. Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy criteria apply only when that category is in scope.
rules.quote: a complete set of criteria consists of (a) the common criteria and (b) the control activity criteria applicable to the specific trust services category or categories addressed by the engagement

rules.summary: Points of focus guide the assessment but are not requirements; ones that do not fit the entity are marked not applicable without affecting the criterion.
rules.quote: Some points of focus may not be suitable or relevant to the entity or to the engagement to be performed.

rules.summary: The 2022 revisions changed points of focus only; the criteria themselves are unchanged from 2017.
rules.quote: The changes to the points of focus in the 2022 revisions do not, in any way, alter the criteria in the 2017 TSC.

sections: Services provided and principal service commitments

glossary.definition: System and Organization Controls 2: an independent examination of a service organization's controls against the AICPA trust services criteria.
American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which publishes the trust services criteria.
Trust services criteria: the AICPA criteria for security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission, whose internal control framework the common criteria build on.
Complementary user entity control: a control the service organization's customers must operate for the system's controls to work as described.

display_name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised points of focus 2022)

controls.title: Integrity and Ethical Values
controls.description: The organization sets and enforces expectations for ethical conduct, including a code of conduct, so that commitments to integrity are demonstrated across the entity.
controls.guidance:
Code of conduct: Maintain a written code of conduct covering ethics, acceptable use, and security responsibilities, acknowledged by every employee and contractor at hire and annually.
Tone at the top: Leadership visibly reinforces ethical and security expectations, and violations are addressed consistently regardless of seniority.
Contractor coverage: Extend conduct and integrity expectations to contractors and temporary staff through onboarding terms and agreements.

objectives.text: Sets the Tone at the Top
objectives.description: Leadership visibly backs ethical and security expectations through its own decisions and messaging, so staff see integrity treated as a priority rather than a slogan.
The organization has a written code of conduct that spells out expected behavior and is shared with staff and relevant outside parties.

objectives.text: Evaluates Adherence to Standards of Conduct
objectives.description: Staff periodically acknowledge the code of conduct, and the organization checks whether people actually follow it through reviews, monitoring or reported issues.

objectives.text: Addresses Deviations in a Timely Manner
objectives.description: Breaches of conduct are investigated and corrected promptly, with consistent consequences applied regardless of the person's role or seniority.

objectives.text: Considers Contractors and Vendor Employees in Demonstrating Its Commitment
objectives.description: Contractors and vendor staff are held to the same ethical and conduct expectations as employees, typically through contracts, onboarding and acknowledgments.

controls.title: Board Oversight
controls.description: Those charged with governance operate independently of management and oversee the development and performance of internal control.
controls.guidance:
Independent oversight: A board, advisory body, or independent owner reviews security program performance on a set cadence.
Oversight of management: Governance reviews management's design and operation of controls rather than relying on management self-reporting.
Security expertise: Governance has access to security expertise, internal or external, sufficient to challenge management.

objectives.description: The board or an equivalent governing body has defined, documented responsibilities for overseeing security, risk and internal control.
Board members collectively have the skills and experience needed to challenge management and oversee security and control matters effectively.
The oversight body includes members independent of management, giving it the objectivity to question decisions and hold executives accountable.
The board brings in outside advisors or specialists when it lacks in-house expertise on topics such as cybersecurity or privacy.

controls.title: Organizational Structure
controls.description: Management defines reporting lines, authorities, and responsibilities appropriate to the entity's objectives.
controls.guidance:
Defined structure: Maintain an org chart with clear reporting lines covering security roles and responsibilities.
Role definitions: Document responsibilities for control operation in role descriptions or a RACI so ownership of each control is unambiguous.
Authority delegation: Delegate authority commensurate with responsibility and periodically review it as the entity changes.

objectives.text: Considers All Structures of the Entity
objectives.description: Management designs its organizational structure across all business units, subsidiaries, locations and outsourced functions so control responsibilities are covered everywhere.
Clear reporting lines exist so each role knows who it answers to and information on security and controls flows to the right decision makers.

objectives.text: Defines, Assigns, and Limits Authorities and Responsibilities
objectives.description: Roles, approval authorities and responsibilities are documented and limited to what each position needs, supporting segregation of duties.

objectives.text: Addresses Specific Requirements When Defining Authorities and Responsibilities
objectives.description: Security, compliance and other specialized responsibilities are explicitly assigned in job descriptions or charters, including any required by law or contract.

objectives.text: Considers Interactions With External Parties When Establishing Structures, Reporting Lines, Authorities, and Responsibilities
objectives.description: The organization defines who is responsible for managing vendors, customers and other external parties that affect its systems and controls.

objectives.text: Establishes Structures, Reporting Lines, and Authorities to Support Compliance With Legal and Contractual Privacy Requirements
objectives.description: A designated privacy function, such as a privacy officer, has clear authority and reporting lines to ensure legal and contractual privacy obligations are met.

controls.title: Competence
controls.description: The organization attracts, develops, and retains people with the skills needed to meet its objectives, including security responsibilities.
controls.guidance:
Hiring standards: Screen candidates per policy (background checks where lawful) and verify competence for security-relevant roles.
Training and development: Provide role-appropriate training so personnel can carry out control responsibilities, refreshed on a defined cadence.
Succession: Identify backups for critical security roles to avoid single points of failure.

objectives.description: Documented hiring, training and performance policies define the skills and competence expected for each role, especially those with security responsibilities.
Management regularly assesses whether staff and providers have the needed competence and takes action, such as training or reassignment, when gaps appear.
The organization recruits, mentors, trains and retains qualified people so it keeps enough capable staff to run its controls.
Succession and backup plans exist for key roles so critical security and control duties continue if someone leaves or is unavailable.
Background checks appropriate to the role's sensitivity are performed on new hires and contractors before they are given access.

objectives.text: Considers the Technical Competency of Individuals
objectives.description: Candidates' technical skills are verified against role requirements during hiring and when people move into technical or security positions.

objectives.text: Provides Training to Maintain Technical Competencies
objectives.description: Staff receive ongoing technical and security training, certifications or education so their skills stay current with technology and threats.

controls.title: Accountability
controls.description: Individuals are held accountable for their internal control responsibilities, with incentives and disciplinary processes aligned to them.
controls.guidance:
Performance accountability: Include control and security responsibilities in performance evaluation for relevant roles.
Incentive alignment: Design incentives that avoid rewarding behavior that undermines controls, and apply discipline consistently for violations.
Escalation: Provide a channel to report control failures and misconduct without fear of retaliation.

objectives.text: Enforces Accountability Through Structures, Authorities, and Responsibilities
objectives.description: Management holds individuals accountable for their control responsibilities, with expectations tracked through the organizational structure and corrective action taken when needed.

objectives.text: Establishes Performance Measures, Incentives, and Rewards
objectives.description: Performance goals, incentives and rewards include security and control responsibilities, not just business results.

objectives.text: Evaluates Performance Measures, Incentives, and Rewards for Ongoing Relevance
objectives.description: Management periodically reviews performance measures and incentives to confirm they still fit current objectives and don't encourage unwanted behavior.
Management watches for unrealistic targets or workload pressures that could push staff to bypass controls and adjusts goals or resources accordingly.

objectives.text: Evaluates Performance and Rewards or Disciplines Individuals
objectives.description: Individual performance reviews cover adherence to security and conduct expectations, leading to recognition or discipline as appropriate.
Staff who mishandle personal information or violate privacy policies face defined, consistently applied disciplinary consequences.

controls.title: Information Quality
controls.description: The organization identifies what information its controls depend on and makes sure that information is accurate, complete, timely and fit for purpose.
controls.guidance:
Data quality: Identify the information internal control depends on (logs, reports, metrics) and validate its completeness and accuracy.
Relevant reporting: Produce security reporting (posture, incidents, exceptions) at a frequency that supports timely decisions.
Source reliability: Prefer system-generated evidence over manual assertions for control monitoring.

objectives.description: The organization defines what information it needs to operate and monitor its controls, and revisits those needs as objectives change.

objectives.text: Captures Internal and External Sources of Data
objectives.description: Relevant data is collected from both internal sources, such as system logs, and external sources, such as threat intelligence and vendor reports.
Raw data is turned into usable information, such as reports, dashboards or alerts, that people can act on to run controls.
Controls keep data accurate, complete and protected as it is collected, processed and stored, so decisions rely on trustworthy information.
Data flow diagrams or similar documentation show how information moves through systems, interfaces and third parties.
A maintained inventory of hardware, software, data and other assets identifies each item and its owner.
Information is labeled by sensitivity, such as public, internal or confidential, so appropriate handling and protection rules apply.

objectives.text: Uses Information That Is Complete and Accurate
objectives.description: Reports and data used to run or test controls are checked for completeness and accuracy before people rely on them.
The organization tracks where its assets and data physically and logically reside, including cloud regions and third-party locations.

controls.title: Internal Communication
controls.description: Objectives, responsibilities, and expectations for internal control, including security commitments, are communicated internally.
controls.guidance:
Policy communication: Publish security policies where personnel can find them and notify on material changes.
Objectives and responsibilities: Communicate each person's control responsibilities at onboarding and when roles change.
Whistleblower channel: Maintain and publicize a confidential channel for reporting concerns.

objectives.description: Policies, procedures and control expectations are communicated to staff so everyone knows how to carry out their control responsibilities.

objectives.text: Communicates With the Board of Directors
objectives.description: Management regularly reports to the board on security, risk and control matters so directors can exercise oversight.
Staff have an alternative, confidential channel, such as an ethics hotline, to raise concerns when normal reporting lines fail or are unsuitable.
Internal communications use methods suited to the audience and message, such as training, intranet posts, meetings or email, considering timing and sensitivity.
Employees and contractors are informed of their specific security and control duties through job descriptions, policies and onboarding.

objectives.text: Communicates Information on Reporting Failures, Incidents, Concerns, and Other Matters
objectives.description: Staff know how and where to report security incidents, system failures, policy violations and other concerns.

objectives.text: Communicates Objectives and Changes to Objectives
objectives.description: Business and security objectives, and any changes to them, are shared with staff who need them to do their jobs.

objectives.text: Communicates Information to Improve Security Knowledge and Awareness
objectives.description: Regular security awareness training and communications keep staff informed about threats such as phishing and their part in preventing them.

objectives.text: Communicates Information to Improve Privacy Knowledge and Awareness
objectives.description: Staff receive privacy training and communications explaining how to handle personal information and meet privacy obligations.
Personnel are told how to report suspected privacy incidents or breaches involving personal information, and to whom.

objectives.text: Communicates Information About System Operation and Boundaries
objectives.description: Internal staff have access to a description of how the system works, what it includes and where its boundaries lie.
The commitments and requirements the system must meet are communicated internally so staff understand what the system is designed to achieve.
Changes to the system that affect staff responsibilities or how work is done are communicated to them in a timely way.

controls.title: External Communication
controls.description: The organization communicates with external parties about matters affecting internal control, such as service commitments, incidents, and changes.
controls.guidance:
Customer commitments: Communicate service commitments, system boundaries, and responsibilities to customers (terms, trust page, SLAs).
Incident communication: Define how and when external parties, including customers and regulators, are notified of incidents.
Vendor expectations: Communicate security expectations to vendors and receive their communications, such as breach notices and SOC reports.

objectives.description: The organization shares relevant control and security information with customers, vendors, regulators and other outside parties.
Customers, vendors and the public have open channels, such as support portals or contact addresses, to send concerns and information to the organization.

objectives.text: Communicates With the Board of Directors
objectives.description: Relevant information from external parties, such as customer complaints or regulator findings, is passed on to the board.
External parties have a confidential or anonymous way, such as a whistleblower line, to report concerns outside normal contacts.
Communications to external parties use methods appropriate to the audience, sensitivity and legal requirements of the message.

objectives.text: Communicates Objectives Related to Confidentiality and Changes to Those Objectives
objectives.description: Confidentiality commitments, and any changes to them, are communicated to customers, vendors and other parties who handle or rely on confidential data.

objectives.text: Communicates Objectives Related to Privacy and Changes to Those Objectives
objectives.description: Privacy commitments, such as privacy notices and their updates, are communicated clearly to data subjects and relevant third parties.
Data subjects and external parties are told how to report privacy incidents, complaints or suspected misuse of personal information.

objectives.text: Communicates Information About System Operation and Boundaries
objectives.description: Customers and other external users receive a description of how the system works and what it does and does not cover.
Customers and relevant external parties are told what the system is designed to achieve and the service commitments it supports.
External users are informed of their own responsibilities, such as complementary user controls, for using the system securely.

objectives.text: Communicates Information on Reporting System Failures, Incidents, Concerns, and Other Matters
objectives.description: Customers and other external users know how to report system outages, security incidents or other concerns, and how those reports are handled.

controls.title: Objective Setting
controls.description: The organization specifies objectives clearly enough that risks to their achievement can be identified and assessed.
controls.guidance:
Objective clarity: State security, availability, and processing objectives specifically enough to assess risk against them.
Commitment linkage: Trace objectives to customer commitments and legal or contractual obligations.
Tolerance definition: Define risk tolerance so deviations from objectives are recognizable.

objectives.description: Leadership deliberately chooses its operational objectives, such as service levels and uptime targets, and documents how they tie to strategy.
Operational objectives state how much variation or underperformance leadership will accept, giving risk assessments a clear threshold to measure against.

objectives.text: Includes Operations and Financial Performance Goals
objectives.description: Objectives cover both operational and financial performance targets, so risk assessments can show which risks threaten service delivery and which threaten results.

objectives.text: Forms a Basis for Committing of Resources
objectives.description: Documented objectives drive where budget, staff and technology are allocated, so investment decisions trace back to stated goals.
Financial reporting objectives are set to meet the accounting standards that apply to the organization, so reporting risks can be judged against them.
Financial reporting objectives account for what size of error or omission would matter to users of the reports, focusing risk work on significant items.
Financial reporting objectives are grounded in the organization's actual transactions and operations, so reports describe what really happens in the business.
Non-financial external reports, such as sustainability or security disclosures, are aligned to the recognized frameworks and standards the organization has adopted.

objectives.text: Considers the Required Level of Precision
objectives.description: Objectives for non-financial external reports define how accurate and detailed the information must be for readers to rely on it.
Non-financial external reports reflect real events and activities across the organization rather than aspirational or selectively chosen information.
Leadership decides what internal reports it needs to run the business, and those choices shape the objectives for internal reporting.

objectives.text: Considers the Required Level of Precision
objectives.description: Internal reports have defined accuracy and detail requirements so managers can rely on them when making decisions.
Internal reporting covers the organization's actual operations and events, giving management an accurate picture of what is happening.
Compliance objectives are built from the laws and regulations that apply to the organization, including aviation, privacy and security requirements.
Leadership defines how much compliance risk it will accept, generally with very little tolerance for breaking laws or regulations.
Top-level objectives are broken down into specific security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity and privacy sub-objectives that risk assessments can target directly.

controls.title: Risk Identification
controls.description: Risks to objectives are identified across the entity and analyzed to determine how they should be managed.
controls.guidance:
Risk register: Maintain a risk register identifying threats to objectives across the entity, systems, and data, with likelihood and impact ratings.
Periodic assessment: Perform the risk assessment on a defined cadence and on significant change.
Treatment decisions: Record how each significant risk is treated: mitigated, accepted, transferred, or avoided, with an owner.

objectives.text: Includes Entity, Subsidiary, Division, Operating Unit, and Functional Levels
objectives.description: Risk identification covers the whole organization, including subsidiaries, divisions, business units and individual functions, not just headquarters or IT.
Risk assessments consider both internal factors, such as staffing and systems, and external ones, such as regulation, economic conditions and threat actors.
Managers at the right levels take part in identifying and analyzing risks, so those closest to each area contribute and own the results.
Identified risks are rated for likelihood and impact using a consistent method, so the organization knows which risks matter most.

objectives.text: Determines How to Respond to Risks
objectives.description: Each significant risk has a documented decision to accept, avoid, reduce or transfer it, with an owner and planned actions.
The organization identifies threats, such as attackers, insiders, outages and natural events, that could stop it from meeting its system objectives.
Weaknesses in infrastructure, software, data, people and processes are identified, for example through vulnerability scans and architecture reviews.

objectives.text: Analyzes Threats and Vulnerabilities From Vendors, Business Partners, and Other Parties
objectives.description: Risk assessments cover threats and weaknesses introduced by vendors, partners and other third parties with access to systems or data.

objectives.text: Assesses the Significance of the Risks
objectives.description: Each risk's potential impact and likelihood are evaluated against objectives to decide which require treatment and how urgently.

controls.title: Fraud Risk
controls.description: The potential for fraud, including unauthorized access and misuse of assets, is considered in assessing risks.
controls.guidance:
Fraud scenarios: Consider fraud explicitly, including unauthorized access, data theft, management override, and misuse of assets.
Incentive review: Assess where incentives and pressures could motivate fraudulent behavior.
Anti-fraud controls: Map fraud risks to the controls that mitigate them, such as segregation of duties and monitoring.

objectives.description: Fraud risk assessments consider fraudulent reporting, theft or misuse of assets, corruption and unauthorized system access.
The organization examines pressures and incentives, such as aggressive targets or bonus structures, that could push people to commit fraud.
The organization identifies where weak controls, excessive access or poor oversight could give someone the chance to commit and conceal fraud.
Fraud assessments consider how individuals might justify misconduct, and whether the culture or past tolerance of wrongdoing makes this more likely.

objectives.text: Considers the Risks Related to the Use of IT and Access to Information
objectives.description: Fraud risk analysis covers how IT systems and access to data could be abused, for example through privileged accounts, data changes or credential misuse.

controls.title: Change Analysis
controls.description: The organization identifies and assesses changes, internal and external, that could significantly affect internal control.
controls.guidance:
Change identification: Identify internal and external changes (new systems, vendors, regulations, threats, business models) that alter risk.
Assessment refresh: Update the risk assessment when significant changes occur rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Leadership review: Review the impact of significant changes on internal control with leadership.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in the External Environment
objectives.description: The organization tracks external changes, such as new regulations, market shifts or geopolitical events, and assesses their effect on controls.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in the Business Model
objectives.description: New products, services, locations, acquisitions or rapid growth trigger a review of whether existing controls still fit the business.
Changes in senior management or key personnel are reviewed for effects on control culture, oversight and knowledge of how controls operate.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in Systems and Technology
objectives.description: New or significantly changed systems, platforms and technologies are assessed for new risks before and after they are introduced.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in Vendor and Business Partner Relationships
objectives.description: New, ended or changed vendor and partner relationships are evaluated for how they shift risk and affect controls.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in Threats and Vulnerabilities
objectives.description: The organization monitors the evolving threat landscape and newly discovered vulnerabilities, and updates its risk assessment when these change.

controls.title: Ongoing Evaluations
controls.description: The organization performs ongoing and separate evaluations to confirm that controls are present and functioning.
controls.guidance:
Monitoring program: Perform ongoing monitoring (metrics, alerts, control self-tests) and periodic evaluations (internal audits, assessments) of control effectiveness.
Independent evaluation: Use evaluators independent of control operators where practicable, including third-party assessments.
Baseline understanding: Establish an understood baseline of control design so deviations are detectable.

objectives.text: Considers a Mix of Ongoing and Separate Evaluations
objectives.description: Monitoring combines continuous, built-in checks with periodic standalone reviews such as internal audits or independent assessments.
The frequency and depth of monitoring increase where the business, systems or risks are changing quickly.
Evaluations start from a documented understanding of how controls are designed and expected to work, so deviations can be recognized.
Control evaluations are performed by people who understand the controls, processes and systems being reviewed.
Ongoing monitoring is embedded in day-to-day operations, such as automated alerts and routine reconciliations, rather than being a separate exercise.
How often and how deeply controls are evaluated is adjusted according to risk, past findings and the significance of each control.
Periodic evaluations are carried out by reviewers independent of the control's operation, such as internal audit or external assessors, to ensure objectivity.

objectives.text: Considers Different Types of Ongoing and Separate Evaluations
objectives.description: The organization uses varied evaluation methods, such as penetration tests, compliance audits, certifications and supplier reviews, to confirm controls are working.

controls.title: Deficiency Communication
controls.description: Control deficiencies are evaluated and communicated to those responsible for corrective action, including senior management and governance as appropriate.
controls.guidance:
Deficiency tracking: Record identified deficiencies with severity, owner, and remediation date, and track to closure.
Escalation of findings: Communicate deficiencies to those able to act, escalating significant ones to senior management and governance.
Remediation verification: Verify remediation effectiveness rather than closing on assertion.

objectives.description: Management or governance reviews the results of control evaluations to determine which issues are deficiencies and how serious they are.
Control deficiencies are reported promptly to the people responsible for fixing them and, when significant, to senior management and the board.
Corrective actions for deficiencies are tracked to completion, with owners, deadlines and verification that the fix actually works.

controls.title: Control Selection
controls.description: Controls are chosen and designed specifically to bring the risks identified in the risk assessment down to a level management is willing to accept.
controls.guidance:
Risk-linked controls: Select and design control activities that directly address risks in the risk register.
Layered approach: Mix preventive, detective, and corrective controls at entity, process, and technology levels.
Segregation of duties: Segregate incompatible duties, applying compensating monitoring where segregation is impracticable.

objectives.description: Control activities are mapped to the risks identified in the risk assessment, so each significant risk has controls designed to address it.
Control design takes into account the organization's size, environment, complexity, regulatory setting and operating model.
The organization identifies which business processes are relevant to its objectives and places controls within those processes.

objectives.text: Evaluates a Mix of Control Activity Types
objectives.description: The control set mixes preventive and detective, manual and automated controls so no single type carries all the risk.

objectives.text: Considers at What Level Activities Are Applied
objectives.description: Controls are applied at appropriate levels, from organization-wide policies down to individual transactions and system functions.
Incompatible duties, such as requesting, approving and executing changes, are split between different people, or compensating controls exist where separation is impractical.

controls.title: Technology Controls
controls.description: General controls over technology are selected and developed to support the achievement of objectives.
controls.guidance:
Technology general controls: Implement general controls over technology: access, change, and operations controls for the infrastructure controls rely on.
Control coverage: Ensure security tooling and infrastructure controls span the full system boundary, including cloud services.
Configuration baselines: Maintain secure configuration baselines for infrastructure supporting control activities.

objectives.text: Determines Dependency Between the Use of Technology in Business Processes and Technology General Controls
objectives.description: The organization understands which business processes rely on technology and ensures general IT controls protect the systems those processes depend on.

objectives.text: Establishes Relevant Technology Infrastructure Control Activities
objectives.description: Controls over networks, servers, databases and other infrastructure ensure systems are complete, accurate and available.

objectives.text: Establishes Relevant Security Management Process Controls Activities
objectives.description: Security controls such as access management, authentication and monitoring protect systems and data from unauthorized access.

objectives.text: Establishes Relevant Technology Acquisition, Development, and Maintenance Process Control Activities
objectives.description: Controls govern how technology is acquired, developed, changed and maintained, including testing, approval and change management.

controls.title: Policy Deployment
controls.description: Control activities are deployed through policies that establish expectations and procedures that put them into action.
controls.guidance:
Policy-to-procedure: Back each policy with procedures naming who performs the activity, how, and how often.
Competent execution: Assign control activities to competent personnel with the authority to perform them.
Periodic reassessment: Reassess policies, procedures, and control activities on a cadence and after incidents or change.

objectives.text: Establishes Policies and Procedures to Support Deployment of Management’s Directives
objectives.description: Documented policies and procedures turn leadership's directives into specific, day-to-day control activities that staff can follow.

objectives.text: Establishes Responsibility and Accountability for Executing Policies and Procedures
objectives.description: Named roles are assigned ownership of carrying out each policy and procedure, and are held accountable for doing so.
Control activities are performed on schedule, so reviews, approvals and checks happen when they are supposed to, not after the fact.
Issues found while performing control activities are investigated and resolved, with follow-up action taken by those responsible.
Control activities are carried out by people with the skills, authority and training needed to perform them properly.
Policies and procedures are reviewed periodically and updated when the business, risks or technology change.

controls.title: Logical Access Security
controls.description: Software, network design and system settings work together to keep protected data and systems open only to authorized people and services.
controls.guidance:
Identity lifecycle: Manage identities from provisioning to deprovisioning in an identity store of record covering employees, contractors, and service accounts.
Authentication strength: Enforce strong authentication: MFA for remote, privileged, and sensitive access; strong credential standards elsewhere.
Asset and data boundaries: Inventory protected information assets and define the system boundary the access controls protect.
Encryption of protected assets: Protect information at rest with encryption or equivalent safeguards aligned to its classification.

objectives.text: Identifies and Manages the Inventory of Information Assets
objectives.description: The organization keeps a current inventory of its systems, data stores and devices, each with an owner and classification, so access controls cover every asset.
New systems, cloud services and design changes are reviewed for access and security implications before they go live, not bolted on afterward.
Access to systems and data is limited to approved users and services through enforced controls such as role-based permissions and deny-by-default settings.
Every person and service is uniquely identified and must prove who they are, for example with passwords and MFA, before reaching protected resources.
Networks are divided into zones so sensitive systems are isolated from general traffic and a compromise in one area cannot spread freely.
Entry points such as VPNs, remote access gateways, APIs and admin consoles are known, limited in number and controlled.
Permissions on individual databases, files and applications are set so users reach only the information their job requires.
Rules for identity and login, such as password strength, MFA, lockout and session timeouts, are defined, applied consistently and kept up to date.

objectives.text: Manages Credentials for Infrastructure and Software
objectives.description: Service accounts, API keys, default passwords and other system credentials are inventoried, stored securely, rotated and never left at vendor defaults.
Sensitive data is encrypted at rest using approved algorithms wherever it is stored, including databases, backups and laptops.
Encryption keys are generated, stored, rotated and retired under controlled procedures, with access limited to a small set of authorized custodians.

objectives.text: Restricts Access to and Use of Confidential Information for Identified Purposes
objectives.description: Access to confidential business information is granted only to people who need it for an approved purpose, and its use is restricted to that purpose.

objectives.text: Restricts Access to and the Use of Personal Information
objectives.description: Personal data is accessible only to staff and systems that need it for the purposes disclosed to individuals, and is not used for anything else.

controls.title: User Registration
controls.description: New internal and external users are registered and authorized before credentials are issued, and access is removed when no longer appropriate.
controls.guidance:
Provisioning approval: Require documented authorization before credentials are issued, tied to role.
Deprovisioning: Remove access promptly on termination or role change, with a defined SLA and verification.
Access recertification: Recertify user access on a cadence, removing access not reaffirmed by owners.

objectives.text: Creates Access Credentials to Protected Information Assets
objectives.description: User accounts and credentials are issued only after a documented request is approved by the appropriate owner or manager.
Active accounts and credentials are reviewed periodically to confirm each one still belongs to a current, authorized user with a valid need.

objectives.text: Prevents the Use of Credentials When No Longer Valid
objectives.description: Accounts and credentials are disabled promptly when someone leaves, changes roles or a contract ends, so stale logins cannot be used.

controls.title: Access Modification and Removal
controls.description: Access to data and system resources is granted, modified, and revoked based on roles and responsibilities, applying least privilege and segregation of duties.
controls.guidance:
Role-based access: Grant access through roles reflecting least privilege and need-to-know; exceptions are documented and time-bound.
Privileged access management: Control privileged access separately: separate accounts, stronger authentication, session logging, and periodic review.
Segregation enforcement: Enforce segregation of duties in entitlements, with compensating monitoring where technical enforcement is not possible.

objectives.text: Creates or Modifies Access to Protected Information Assets
objectives.description: Granting or changing a user's access follows an approved request tied to their role, with records kept of who authorized it.

objectives.text: Removes Access to Protected Information Assets
objectives.description: Access is revoked in a timely, tracked way when it is no longer needed, such as at termination, transfer or project completion.
Access is organized through defined roles or groups that enforce least privilege and keep conflicting duties separated.
Roles, group memberships and access rules are reviewed on a schedule by owners, and excess or conflicting permissions are corrected.

controls.title: Physical Access
controls.description: Only authorized people can enter data centers, server rooms, media storage and other sensitive places, and that access is withdrawn when it is no longer needed.
controls.guidance:
Facility access: Restrict physical access to facilities and sensitive areas to authorized personnel with badge or equivalent controls.
Visitor management: Log and escort visitors in areas containing protected assets.
Physical access review: Review and revoke physical access rights on the same lifecycle as logical access.

objectives.description: Badges, keys or entry rights to secure facilities are issued or changed only after documented approval based on job need.
Physical access rights are withdrawn promptly when people leave or no longer need entry, including deactivating badges and collecting keys.
Badges, keys, laptops and other company devices are collected back from departing staff and contractors.
Lists of who can enter secure areas, and entry logs, are reviewed periodically and unneeded access is removed.

controls.title: Asset Disposal
controls.description: Protected information is removed from assets and media before disposal or repurposing.
controls.guidance:
Sanitization before disposal: Sanitize or destroy media and equipment containing protected information before disposal or reuse, with certificates where third parties perform it.
Decommissioning process: Formally decommission systems: remove data, revoke credentials and certificates, and update inventories.

objectives.text: Removes Data and Software for Disposal
objectives.description: Data and software are securely wiped or the media physically destroyed before equipment is discarded, resold or reused, with records of disposal kept.

controls.title: External Threat Protection
controls.description: The organization implements measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.
controls.guidance:
Perimeter defenses: Defend external boundaries with firewalls, hardened endpoints, and controlled ingress and egress.
Remote access security: Secure remote access via encrypted channels with MFA, avoiding split exposure of internal resources.
External threat monitoring: Monitor external-facing services for attack and abuse, including credential stuffing and scanning.

objectives.description: Connections from outside the network are limited to approved sources, protocols and ports, with everything else blocked.
Passwords, tokens and other credentials used over external connections are protected from interception, for example through encryption and secure storage.
Remote and higher-risk access, such as VPN, admin or third-party logins, requires an extra factor or step beyond a password.
Firewalls, web gateways, intrusion prevention and similar tools guard the network perimeter and are configured and maintained to block threats.

controls.title: Data in Transit and on Devices
controls.description: The movement of information to and from the system, and its handling on removable media and end-user devices, is restricted and protected.
controls.guidance:
Transmission encryption: Encrypt protected information in transit over public and untrusted networks with current protocols.
Endpoint and media controls: Restrict movement of protected data to removable media and unmanaged endpoints; encrypt and manage what is allowed.
Data loss prevention: Apply controls to detect or block unauthorized exfiltration channels appropriate to risk.

objectives.text: Restricts the Ability to Perform Transmission
objectives.description: Only authorized users and systems can send data out of the environment, with controls such as DLP or restricted file-sharing limiting transfers.

objectives.text: Uses Encryption Technologies or Secure Communication Channels to Protect Data
objectives.description: Data moving across networks is protected with encryption such as TLS or VPN tunnels, especially over public or untrusted links.
USB drives and other removable media are restricted, encrypted when allowed, and tracked to prevent data loss.
Laptops, phones and workstations are protected with measures like disk encryption, screen locks, device management and remote wipe.

controls.title: Unauthorized Software
controls.description: Controls prevent and detect the introduction of unauthorized or malicious software.
controls.guidance:
Malware defense: Deploy anti-malware or endpoint detection on susceptible systems, kept current and centrally monitored.
Software allowlisting: Control what software can be introduced and executed, through allowlisting, signing, or managed distribution.
Unauthorized software detection: Detect unauthorized software through inventory reconciliation or endpoint telemetry.

objectives.text: Restricts Installation and Modification of Application and Software
objectives.description: Only authorized personnel can install or change software, with users blocked from adding unapproved applications.

objectives.text: Detects Unauthorized Changes to Software and Configuration Parameters
objectives.description: Tools such as file integrity monitoring alert staff when software or configuration settings change without authorization.

objectives.text: Uses a Defined Change Control Process
objectives.description: Software and configuration changes go through a documented process of request, testing, approval and deployment.
Anti-malware or endpoint protection runs on servers and endpoints, stays updated and alerts on detected threats.

objectives.text: Scans Information Assets From Outside the Entity for Malware and Other Unauthorized Software
objectives.description: Files, email attachments and devices arriving from outside are scanned for malware or unapproved software before being allowed in.

controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring
controls.description: The organization monitors its infrastructure and software for vulnerabilities and configuration deviations that could expose the system.
controls.guidance:
Vulnerability scanning: Scan infrastructure and applications for vulnerabilities on a cadence and after significant change, remediating by risk-based SLAs.
Configuration monitoring: Detect deviations from secure configuration baselines.
Threat intelligence: Track new vulnerabilities and threats relevant to the technology stack.

objectives.description: Systems are built and maintained against documented hardening baselines, and deviations from those standards are identified and fixed.
Infrastructure and applications are continuously monitored for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and signs of weakness.
Automated tools flag changes to critical files, settings or infrastructure so unexpected modifications are noticed and investigated.
The environment is regularly checked for unknown devices, software or cloud resources, and anything unauthorized is investigated and removed.
Internal and external vulnerability scans run on a regular schedule and after major changes, with findings tracked to remediation.

controls.title: Anomaly Detection
controls.description: System components are monitored for anomalies and security events that could indicate malicious acts, natural disasters, or errors.
controls.guidance:
Security monitoring: Collect and analyze security-relevant logs across the boundary; alert on anomalies indicating incidents, errors, or misuse.
Coverage completeness: Ensure monitoring covers critical systems, identity providers, and cloud control planes, not just servers.
Alert triage: Define who reviews alerts, how fast, and how false positives are tuned.

objectives.text: Implements Detection Policies, Procedures, and Tools
objectives.description: Documented monitoring procedures and tools, such as logging, SIEM and alerting, are in place to spot suspicious activity.
Monitoring is designed around known threats and critical assets so it catches unauthorized access, malware and unusual behavior.
Logs and events are filtered, correlated and analyzed to separate real anomalies from normal activity and noise.

objectives.text: Monitors Detection Tools for Effective Operation
objectives.description: Detection tools are checked regularly to confirm they are running, collecting data and generating alerts as intended.

controls.title: Event Evaluation
controls.description: Alerts and suspicious activity are triaged to decide whether they are real incidents that put commitments at risk, and confirmed incidents are acted on.
controls.guidance:
Event evaluation: Assess detected events against incident criteria to decide whether objectives were or could be affected.
Severity classification: Classify incidents by impact to drive proportionate response.
Lessons captured: Record evaluation outcomes, including non-incidents, to improve detection.

objectives.description: Confirmed security incidents are handled through a defined response process with assigned owners and tracked actions.

objectives.text: Communicates and Reviews Detected Security Events
objectives.description: Detected security events are reported to the right people and reviewed to decide whether they warrant incident handling.

objectives.text: Develops and Implements Procedures to Analyze Security Incidents
objectives.description: Written procedures guide how staff investigate events to determine their cause, scope and severity.

objectives.text: Assesses the Impact on Confidential Information
objectives.description: When an incident occurs, the organization determines whether confidential business information was affected and how seriously.

objectives.text: Determines Confidential Information Used or Disclosed
objectives.description: Investigations establish exactly which confidential information was accessed, used or disclosed without authorization.

objectives.text: Assesses the Impact on Personal Information
objectives.description: Incidents are evaluated to determine whether personal data was involved and what harm could result for the individuals concerned.

objectives.text: Determines Personal Information Used or Disclosed
objectives.description: Investigations identify which personal data records and individuals were exposed, used or disclosed improperly.

controls.title: Incident Response
controls.description: The organization responds to identified security incidents through an established program of containment, remediation, and communication.
controls.guidance:
Incident response program: Operate a documented incident response process: roles, containment, eradication, communication, and legal or regulatory notification.
Response testing: Exercise the plan (tabletops or simulations) at least annually and after material change.
Notification obligations: Map notification duties to customers and regulators with their deadlines, and meet them during response.

objectives.description: Incident response roles, such as incident lead, technical responders and communications, are named and understood in advance.

objectives.text: Contains and Responds to Security Incidents
objectives.description: Responders follow defined steps to contain an incident and limit its spread, such as isolating systems or disabling accounts.
Active incidents are mitigated in real time to reduce ongoing damage while the full response continues.
Incidents are worked through to closure, with the threat eliminated and resolution documented before the case is closed.
Affected systems and services are brought back into normal operation in a controlled way after containment.

objectives.text: Develops and Implements Communication of Security Incidents
objectives.description: A plan defines who is told about incidents, when and how, covering management, customers, regulators and other stakeholders.

objectives.text: Obtains Understanding of Nature of Incident and Determines Containment Strategy
objectives.description: Responders analyze what happened and how far it reaches before choosing a containment approach suited to the incident.
Weaknesses exploited or uncovered during an incident are fixed, for example through patching or configuration changes.
Progress and results of remediation work are shared with management and other affected parties.

objectives.text: Evaluates the Effectiveness of Incident Response
objectives.description: After incidents, the organization reviews how well its response worked and updates the plan based on what it learned.
Incident records are reviewed periodically for trends and recurring issues that signal broader control weaknesses.
A defined breach procedure is followed when personal data is compromised, including legal and regulatory notification deadlines.
Individuals, regulators and other required parties are informed when personal data has been used or disclosed without authorization.
Staff or third parties who mishandle personal data face disciplinary or contractual consequences that are applied consistently.

controls.title: Incident Recovery
controls.description: After an incident, the organization restores affected systems and data, confirms normal operation and puts lessons learned into practice.
controls.guidance:
Recovery execution: Restore affected systems and data to known-good state, verifying integrity before return to service.
Root cause and improvement: Perform post-incident review, fix root causes, and feed changes back into controls and training.
Recovery capability: Maintain and test backups and recovery procedures supporting incident recovery.

objectives.description: Systems and data affected by an incident are restored from trusted sources, such as clean backups or rebuilt images, and verified.
Relevant details about the incident and recovery are shared with management, staff and affected external parties as appropriate.

objectives.text: Determines Root Cause of the Incident
objectives.description: Each significant incident is investigated to find its underlying cause, not just the immediate symptoms.

objectives.text: Implements Changes to Prevent and Detect Recurrences
objectives.description: Control or system changes are made after an incident so the same problem is less likely to happen again and easier to detect.
Response and recovery procedures are updated with lessons learned from incidents and exercises.
Recovery plans are tested regularly through exercises or restore tests to confirm systems can actually be brought back.

controls.title: Change Management
controls.description: Changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures are authorized, designed, developed, tested, approved, and implemented in a controlled manner.
controls.guidance:
Change process: Authorize, test, and approve changes to infrastructure, software, and configurations before deployment, with records.
Segregated environments: Separate development, test, and production; restrict who can deploy to production.
Emergency changes: Allow expedited emergency changes with retrospective review and approval.
Infrastructure as code: Apply the same change discipline to infrastructure and configuration changes as to application code.

objectives.text: Manages Changes Throughout the System Life Cycle
objectives.description: Changes are governed by one consistent process from initial request through design, build, release and retirement of system components.
Each change request is reviewed and given permission to proceed by an appropriate owner before any work on it begins.
Changes are designed and built to agreed requirements and coding standards, in environments kept separate from live production systems.
Each change has a written record of what is changing, why, who is involved, and how it was built and verified.
A ticketing or change log tracks every system change and its current status so nothing reaches production untracked.
Software and system settings are configured to approved, hardened standards, and configuration changes follow the same controlled process.
Changes are tested in a non-production environment, with results recorded, before they are allowed into the live system.
A designated authority reviews test results and signs off on each change before it is released to production.
Approved changes are released to production in a controlled way, with rollback plans and checks that deployment succeeded.
The organization identifies needed changes and evaluates their security, operational and business impact before deciding whether to proceed.

objectives.text: Identifies Changes in Infrastructure, Data, Software, and Procedures Required to Remediate Incidents
objectives.description: Lessons from security incidents feed into the change process, so fixes to systems, data, software or procedures are identified and made.

objectives.text: Creates Baseline Configuration of IT Technology
objectives.description: Documented standard configurations exist for servers, network devices and endpoints, and systems are compared against them to spot drift.

objectives.text: Provides for Changes Necessary in Emergency Situations
objectives.description: A defined fast-track path lets urgent fixes go in quickly, with authorization and documentation completed afterward.
Security patches and updates are identified, prioritized, tested and applied within set timeframes through the change process.
Changes are assessed for their effect on uptime and recovery, so updates do not weaken redundancy or availability of the system.
Change work keeps confidential data protected, for example by keeping real sensitive data out of test environments or masking it.
Changes are reviewed so personal information stays protected, such as avoiding live personal data in development and testing.
Privacy requirements are built into new systems and changes from the start, limiting personal data collection and exposure by default.

controls.title: Risk Mitigation
controls.description: The organization plans for events that could interrupt the business, such as outages or disasters, and puts measures in place to limit their impact.
controls.guidance:
Business disruption risk: Identify disruption scenarios (loss of facility, provider, key personnel, data) and mitigate per business impact.
Resilience planning: Maintain continuity and disaster recovery arrangements aligned to recovery objectives.
Insurance and transfer: Consider risk transfer, including cyber insurance, where mitigation alone is insufficient.

objectives.text: Considers Mitigation of Risks of Business Disruption
objectives.description: The organization plans for disruptive events and puts measures such as continuity and recovery arrangements in place to limit business impact.

objectives.text: Considers the Use of Insurance to Mitigate Financial Impact Risks
objectives.description: Leadership evaluates whether insurance, such as cyber or business interruption cover, should absorb part of the financial loss from major incidents.

controls.title: Vendor Risk Management
controls.description: Vendors and business partners are vetted before onboarding and monitored afterwards, so the risks they introduce stay understood and under control.
controls.guidance:
Vendor inventory and tiering: Maintain a vendor inventory tiered by access to systems and data and criticality to operations.
Pre-engagement diligence: Assess vendor security before engagement, proportionate to tier (SOC reports, questionnaires, certifications).
Contractual requirements: Bind vendors to security, confidentiality, and breach notification obligations in contracts.
Ongoing monitoring: Reassess vendors periodically and on trigger events; track remediation of identified issues.

objectives.text: Establishes Requirements for Vendor and Business Partner Engagements
objectives.description: Security, service and compliance expectations for vendors and partners are defined up front and written into contracts or agreements.
The organization identifies weaknesses that vendors and partners could introduce, such as insecure connections, products or access to its data.

objectives.text: Assesses Vendor and Business Partner Risks
objectives.description: Vendors and partners are risk-assessed before onboarding and periodically after, scaled to their access to systems and data.

objectives.text: Assigns Responsibility and Accountability for Managing Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: Named owners are responsible for each vendor or partner relationship, including oversight of security, performance and contract obligations.

objectives.text: Establishes Communication Protocols for Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: Agreed channels and contacts exist for exchanging information with vendors and partners, including how security incidents get reported both ways.

objectives.text: Establishes Exception Handling Procedures From Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: There is a defined process for handling vendor or partner shortfalls, deviations from agreed terms, or requests for exceptions.

objectives.text: Assesses Vendor and Business Partner Performance
objectives.description: Vendor and partner performance against service levels and security obligations is reviewed regularly, using reports, audits or attestations.

objectives.text: Implements Procedures for Addressing Issues Identified During Vendor and Business Partner Assessments
objectives.description: Issues found during vendor reviews are recorded, followed up with the vendor, and tracked until fixed or formally accepted.

objectives.text: Implements Procedures for Terminating Vendor and Business Partner Relationships
objectives.description: Ending a vendor relationship follows a defined process covering revoking access, returning or destroying data, and transitioning services.

objectives.text: Obtains Confidentiality Commitments From Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: Vendors and partners who handle confidential information sign agreements binding them to protect it and limit its use and disclosure.

objectives.text: Assesses Compliance With Confidentiality Commitments of Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: The organization checks that vendors and partners actually honor their confidentiality obligations, through reviews, attestations or audits.

objectives.text: Obtains Privacy Commitments From Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: Vendors and partners that process personal information commit in writing to privacy obligations consistent with the organization's own commitments.

objectives.text: Assesses Compliance With Privacy Commitments of Vendors and Business Partners
objectives.description: The organization verifies that vendors and partners handle personal information as their privacy commitments require, and acts on gaps.

controls.title: Capacity Management
controls.description: Current processing capacity and usage are monitored and evaluated so that capacity demand can be met and future needs planned.
controls.guidance:
Capacity monitoring: Monitor utilization of compute, storage, and network against thresholds that trigger action before service is degraded.
Demand forecasting: Project future capacity needs from growth trends and planned launches, and provision ahead of demand.
Scaling mechanisms: Use scaling arrangements (auto-scaling, headroom, burst capacity) appropriate to the architecture and availability commitments.

objectives.description: System capacity such as compute, storage and network usage is monitored continuously against defined thresholds to keep services available.
Future capacity needs are projected from usage trends and planned business growth so shortfalls are anticipated before they affect availability.
Capacity forecasts lead to concrete actions, such as adding resources or rebalancing workloads, before demand outstrips supply.

controls.title: Environmental and Recovery Infrastructure
controls.description: Environmental protections, backup processes, and recovery infrastructure are designed, implemented, operated, and maintained to meet availability objectives.
controls.guidance:
Environmental protections: Protect infrastructure against environmental hazards (power loss, fire, water, temperature) directly or through hosting providers' certified controls.
Backup regime: Back up data on a schedule aligned to recovery point objectives, protect backups from tampering, and monitor job success.
Recovery infrastructure: Maintain recovery arrangements (redundancy, failover, restore procedures) sized to recovery time objectives.

objectives.description: Environmental risks to facilities and equipment, such as fire, flood, power loss and overheating, are identified and assessed.
Facilities have measures in place to detect environmental problems, such as smoke, water, temperature and humidity sensors.

objectives.text: Implements and Maintains Environmental Protection Mechanisms
objectives.description: Protective equipment such as fire suppression, UPS, generators and cooling is installed, serviced and kept in working order.
Environmental monitoring raises alerts on abnormal conditions so staff can investigate and act before systems are affected.
Documented procedures guide staff in responding to environmental events to protect equipment and restore normal operations.

objectives.text: Communicates and Reviews Detected Environmental Threat Events
objectives.description: Environmental incidents are reported to the right people and reviewed afterward to improve protections and response.
The organization identifies which systems and data must be backed up, and how often, based on business and recovery needs.
Backups run on a defined schedule, are monitored for success, and failures are investigated and corrected.
Backup copies are kept at a separate, protected location, physical or cloud, so a single site loss cannot destroy them.
Secondary or redundant infrastructure is available so critical processing can continue or resume if the primary environment fails.
Recovery objectives are defined and backup and replication approaches are chosen so data can be restored within acceptable loss limits.

controls.title: Recovery Testing
controls.description: Recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery are tested to help meet availability objectives.
controls.guidance:
Restore testing: Test restoration from backups on a cadence, verifying data integrity and completeness, not just job completion.
Failover exercises: Exercise failover and recovery procedures for critical services and record results.
Test-driven improvement: Feed recovery test failures and timing misses back into plan and architecture changes.

objectives.description: The business continuity and disaster recovery plans are exercised regularly, with results reviewed and the plans updated accordingly.

objectives.text: Tests Integrity and Completeness of Backup Data
objectives.description: Restores from backup are tested periodically to confirm the data comes back complete, uncorrupted and usable.

controls.title: Confidential Information Identification
controls.description: Information designated as confidential is identified and maintained to meet the entity's confidentiality objectives.
controls.guidance:
Confidentiality identification: Identify and label information subject to confidentiality commitments at ingestion or creation.
Handling requirements: Define handling requirements (access, storage, sharing, retention) per confidentiality classification.
Commitment traceability: Trace confidentiality obligations from contracts and NDAs to the systems and data they cover.

objectives.description: The organization defines what counts as confidential information and identifies and labels it as it is created or received.
Confidential information is kept only for the period required by commitments, contracts or law, under a defined retention schedule.
Confidential information is safeguarded against accidental or unauthorized deletion or loss while it must still be retained.

controls.title: Confidential Information Disposal
controls.description: Confidential information is disposed of when the retention purpose ends, in a manner that meets confidentiality objectives.
controls.guidance:
Retention-driven disposal: Dispose of confidential information when retention periods lapse or obligations end, on a schedule rather than ad hoc.
Verifiable destruction: Use destruction methods that prevent reconstruction, with certificates or logs as evidence.
Third-party copies: Ensure vendors and processors destroy or return confidential information at engagement end.

objectives.description: Confidential information that has reached the end of its retention period is identified and flagged for disposal on a regular basis.
Confidential information is disposed of securely, using methods such as wiping, shredding or crypto-erasure, with records of destruction kept.

controls.title: Processing Specifications
controls.description: The organization documents what data its services process and how processing should work, and shares that information so the services are used correctly.
controls.guidance:
Data definitions: Document the data processed, its sources, and the specifications the processing must meet.
Specification communication: Make processing specifications available to the personnel and customers who rely on them.
Definition change control: Version and communicate changes to data definitions and processing specifications.

objectives.text: Identifies Functional and Nonfunctional Requirements and Information Specifications
objectives.description: The organization documents what the system must do and how it must perform, including the data it needs to process correctly.

objectives.text: Defines Data Necessary to Support a Product or Service
objectives.description: The data required to deliver each product or service, including its sources, format and quality, is defined and documented.

objectives.text: Defines Information Necessary to Support the Use of a Good or Product
objectives.description: Users are given the information they need to use the product or service correctly, such as specifications, instructions and limitations.

controls.title: Input Completeness and Accuracy
controls.description: System inputs are complete and accurate, and input errors are captured and addressed.
controls.guidance:
Input validation: Validate inputs for completeness, accuracy, and authorization at entry, rejecting or quarantining failures.
Error handling: Capture input errors with enough context to correct and reprocess them.
Source reconciliation: Reconcile received inputs against source counts or control totals where feasible.

objectives.description: Required characteristics of incoming data, such as format, completeness, valid ranges and sources, are defined for each input.
Inputs are validated against defined rules when received, and errors or rejected items are flagged and corrected.

objectives.text: Creates and Maintains Records of System Inputs
objectives.description: Records of data entering the system are kept, showing what was received, when and from where, to support reconciliation.

controls.title: Processing Completeness and Accuracy
controls.description: System processing is complete, accurate, timely, and authorized, with deviations identified and resolved.
controls.guidance:
Processing controls: Enforce completeness and accuracy through the pipeline with control totals, sequence checks, and idempotency safeguards.
Exception management: Detect, log, and resolve processing deviations within defined timeframes.
Authorized processing: Permit processing to run only under authorized schedules, versions, and configurations.

objectives.description: The organization documents how data must be processed, including the rules, calculations and expected outputs for each function.
The processing steps, schedules and responsibilities for each system activity are defined so work runs consistently.

objectives.text: Detects and Corrects Processing or Production Activity Errors
objectives.description: Processing errors and failed jobs are detected through checks and monitoring, then investigated and corrected in a timely manner.
System processing activity is logged so what ran, when and with what result can be traced and reviewed.
Inputs are processed completely, accurately and on time according to the defined specifications.

controls.title: Output Delivery
controls.description: System outputs are complete, accurate, distributed only to intended parties, and protected during delivery.
controls.guidance:
Output verification: Verify outputs for completeness and accuracy before release, reconciling against processed inputs.
Distribution control: Deliver outputs only to defined recipients over protected channels.
Output retention: Retain outputs and delivery evidence per policy to support inquiry and rework.

objectives.description: System outputs such as reports and files are protected from unauthorized access, change or loss.

objectives.text: Distributes Output Only to Intended Parties
objectives.description: Outputs are delivered only to authorized recipients, with controls that confirm the correct destination before release.
Checks such as reconciliations and control totals confirm that outputs are delivered in full and without errors.

objectives.text: Creates and Maintains Records of System Output Activities
objectives.description: Records of output generation and distribution are kept, showing what was sent, to whom and when.

controls.title: Stored Data Integrity
controls.description: Data stored by the system is protected and maintained completely and accurately for its specified retention period.
controls.guidance:
Storage integrity: Protect stored data against unauthorized alteration with access controls, checksums, or immutability where warranted.
Retention execution: Store data for its specified retention period and dispose of it at expiry.
Archival recovery: Ensure archived data remains retrievable and readable for its retention life.

objectives.description: Data and items held in storage are protected from unauthorized access, change, theft or damage.
System records are archived on a defined basis and protected so they remain intact and retrievable when needed.
Stored data is checked to remain complete and accurate, with integrity controls that catch corruption or unintended changes.

objectives.text: Creates and Maintains Records of System Storage Activities
objectives.description: Records of storage activities, such as data being written, changed, moved or deleted, are kept and available for review.

controls.title: Privacy Notice
controls.description: Notice is provided to data subjects about the entity's privacy practices, and is updated and communicated when practices change.
controls.guidance:
Notice content: Publish a privacy notice covering what is collected, purposes, disclosures, retention, and data subject rights.
Notice availability: Make the notice available at or before collection and keep it accessible.
Notice maintenance: Review the notice on a cadence and on practice changes; communicate material updates.

objectives.description: The organization tells individuals what personal information it handles, why, and how they can reach it with privacy questions or concerns.
Individuals receive a privacy notice at or before the point their personal information is collected, or as soon as practical afterward.

objectives.text: Covers Entities and Activities in Notice
objectives.description: The privacy notice names which business units, affiliates, websites, and processing activities it applies to, so nothing in scope is left unexplained.

objectives.text: Uses Clear Language and Presents a Current Privacy Notice in a Location Easily Found by Data Subjects
objectives.description: Privacy notices are written in plain wording, kept up to date, and posted where individuals can easily find them, such as a website footer or signup page.
The organization reviews its privacy notice on a set schedule and whenever practices change, confirming it still matches how data is actually handled.
When the privacy notice changes, the organization alerts affected individuals in advance or promptly, explaining what changed and how it affects them.
Earlier versions of the privacy notice are archived with their effective dates, so the organization can show which terms applied at any point.

controls.title: Choice and Consent
controls.description: Data subjects are informed about choices available to them, and consent for collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal is obtained where required.
controls.guidance:
Choice presentation: Present choices about collection and use clearly, without dark patterns, where choices are offered or required.
Consent capture: Capture and store consent with who, when, what version, and scope.
Consent withdrawal: Provide a withdrawal path as easy as the grant, and honor it across systems.

objectives.description: Individuals are told what choices they have about how their personal information is collected, used, shared, and kept, and how to exercise them.

objectives.text: Communicates Consequences of Denying or Withdrawing Consent
objectives.description: Individuals learn what happens if they refuse or later withdraw consent, such as losing access to certain services or features.
The organization captures consent before relying on personal information, using opt-in or opt-out mechanisms appropriate to the data and applicable law.

objectives.text: Documents and Obtains Consent for New Purposes and Uses
objectives.description: Before reusing personal information for a purpose not originally disclosed, the organization records the new use and gets fresh consent where required.

objectives.text: Obtains Explicit Consent for Sensitive Information
objectives.description: Sensitive data such as health, biometric, or financial details is only collected or used after individuals give clear, affirmative, documented consent.
Individuals agree before their personal information is transferred to other parties or across borders, and that consent is recorded.

controls.title: Collection Limitation
controls.description: Personal information collection is limited to what is consistent with the entity's privacy objectives.
controls.guidance:
Minimal collection: Collect only personal information needed for stated purposes; challenge fields that lack a purpose.
Collection review: Review collection points periodically for scope creep.
Lawful means: Collect by lawful, fair means consistent with the notice.

objectives.text: Limits the Collection of Personal Information
objectives.description: The organization collects only the personal information needed for its stated purposes, and data-gathering forms and systems avoid asking for extras.

objectives.text: Collects Information by Fair and Lawful Means
objectives.description: Personal information is gathered honestly and legally, without deception, hidden tracking, or coercion, and collection methods are reviewed for compliance.
